done.why: I read the prose and sampled the opening area, then stopped early. I had no clear goal beyond a locked chest and an unseen watcher.

about: A Zork-like underground empire. You arrive as a returning adventurer at the foot of an endless stair for a final test. A sword is stuck in a rock, a sunlit cliff oasis lies to the west, and an unseen figure toys with you from above.

moments.note: Moving south put me in the dark with the classic grue warning, and the lantern was needed.
The rock description says it 'has the look of a thing that has been invited many times'.
On the ledge, the rope twitches and a chuckle comes from above, so something unseen is toying with me.
'call up to whoever is there' gave 'You can't see any such thing', so the parser rejected a natural phrase.

wished: Talk to the unseen watcher at the top of the rope.
Find out what the final test is.

lines.line: The rock has the look of a thing that has been invited many times.
lines.why: A dry, characterful line that makes the sword puzzle feel worn and human.

lines.line: Somebody is at the top of this rope, and is in no hurry to say so.
lines.why: It builds menace and patience out of very little.

fun.why: Short but pleasing, with small reactive details such as the rope twitching and the chuckle.

engagement.why: The unseen watcher is a good hook.

difficulty.why: I saw too little to judge. Nothing was blocking me early, apart from a parser miss.

interestingness.why: It builds on a familiar Zork setting and adds a mystery figure and a dream frame.

prose.why: The examine text is wry and precise, and it adds to the original room descriptions rather than repeating them.
